citation.title: DNN-Based Topology Optimisation: Spatial Invariance and Neural Tangent Kernel
citation.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34 (NeurIPS 2021), 27659-27669
citation.version_coded: arXiv v3 (28 Nov 2021), HTML incl. Appendices A-F; the NeurIPS 2021 proceedings PDF (version of record, 11 pp.) was also read, and its main text matches

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: None: the article reports no speed or quality comparison with a classical method. Its experiments compare DNN density parameterizations with and without the proposed coordinate embeddings (Figs. 4, 8-9).
claim.alternatives: Sec. 3.1 (theory): in the wide-network limit, NN-parameterized SIMP behaves like filtered SIMP whose filter is the matrix square root of the limiting NTK; an analogy, not a performance comparison. Sec. 1 cites ref. [7] for DNN density fields lacking the checkerboards of unfiltered SIMP; background, not the article's own result.

notes: Screening code was I-UNCLEAR. The full text (arXiv v3 incl. appendices, and the NeurIPS version of record) contains no classical-baseline result. The Modified Filtering method without a DNN is defined in Sec. 2.2 to allow a comparison, but no results for it are reported. All empirical comparisons are ML versus ML: embedded versus non-embedded fully connected networks (Fig. 4) and up-sampling artifacts without an embedding (Figs. 8-9). Tally under ML-only (PROTOCOL §4, C4). No compliance values or run times are reported. Code: github.com/benjiDupuis/DeepTopo exists (GitHub API, 2026-09-24) with no declared licence.
